title: Act III, Scene III

teacherSummary.text: At dusk a mysterious Third Murderer joins the first two. Banquo and Fleance approach on foot from the palace gate with a torch. The murderers attack and kill Banquo, who cries to Fleance to fly and avenge him. The light is struck out and Fleance escapes. The murderers go to report how much is done.

writingPrompts.label: HS Freshman
writingPrompts.text: In Act III, Scene III, how does Shakespeare develop the idea of Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape? State a clear claim, support it with two or three quotations, and explain how the setting in the scene helps build that idea.

writingPrompts.label: HS Sophomore
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how Act III, Scene III develops the idea of Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of setting and irony shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: HS Junior
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how the structure of Act III, Scene III (where it begins, turns and ends) and its setting shape the reader's understanding of Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape. Identify one place where the text leaves matters uncertain and explain how that uncertainty adds to its meaning.

writingPrompts.label: HS Senior
writingPrompts.text: Two readers disagree about what Act III, Scene III suggests about Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape. Lay out two plausible interpretations, weigh the evidence for each (including the scene's setting and irony), and argue for the stronger one in a sustained, well-organized essay.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how William Shakespeare uses setting in Act III, Scene III to complicate the reader's understanding of Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate Act III, Scene III within its historical and literary context and argue how the scene's treatment of Banquo's murder and Fleance's escape responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “The west yet glimmers with some streaks of day” slowly and put it in my own words: The First Murderer says the west still glimmers with streaks of day. Next, craft. I notice the gentle, poetic description from a hired killer. The strongest word is “glimmers”: it shows the last light before darkness, as Banquo's life is about to end. Then, effect. Why does the murderer describe the fading light? My answer: The fading light marks Banquo's death; the beauty of the line contrasts with the violence to come.
